Table

A rounded, bordered box for an ordinary HTML table — you write the rows, it styles them, and any cell can hold another component. Every table in these docs wears the same classes.

2 sizesSlot-basedToken-driven

Props

Read from interface Props in Table.astro, so it cannot drift from the component.
PropTypeDefaultNotes
size'md' | 'sm''md'Cell padding — md is the reference's 24 across and 16 down; sm is 16 by 12 for dense reference tables.
labelstring—Names the table for assistive tech when no visible heading does.
classstring—Extra classes on the scroll box, applied after the component's own.

Code

          
<Table label="Products">
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col">Product name</th><th scope="col">Category</th><th scope="col">Price</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">IronPDF</th><td>PDF</td><td><Badge intent="success">$749</Badge></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</Table>

<!-- dense reference tables -->
<Table size="sm">…</Table>

Guidelines

✓ Do
  • Put scope="row" on the cell that names its row — it is styled as the row header and read out with every cell.
  • Give the table a label when no visible heading names it.
  • Use a table for data a reader compares across rows and columns.
✗ Don't
  • Don't use a table to lay out a page or a form — use grid or flex.
  • Don't restyle cells with one-off classes; if a table needs a new look, it needs a new size or prop.
  • Don't put the header row in <tbody> — it loses the header fill and the header semantics together.
